source.name: Lichess puzzle database
source.note: Positions and solutions come from the Lichess puzzle database, which is engine-verified and released under CC0. Each puzzle shows the position after the opponent’s move, so the reader is to move.

topics.label: Fork
topics.blurb: One piece attacks two targets at the same time — only one can be saved.

topics.label: Pin
topics.blurb: A piece cannot move because something more valuable sits behind it.

topics.label: Skewer
topics.blurb: The valuable piece is in front and must move, exposing what stands behind it.

topics.label: Discovered attack
topics.blurb: Stepping one piece out of the way unmasks the piece behind it.

topics.label: Double check
topics.blurb: Two pieces give check at once, so the king must run — nothing else helps.

topics.label: Back-rank mate
topics.blurb: A boxed-in king is mated along its own back rank.

topics.label: Mate in two
topics.blurb: A forcing first move leaves Black no defence against mate next move.

topics.label: Hanging piece
topics.blurb: An undefended piece is simply there to be taken.

topics.label: Deflection
topics.blurb: A defender is dragged away from the square it was guarding.

topics.label: Sacrifice
topics.blurb: Material is given up now for something bigger — usually mate or the queen.
